notes.claim: Portable table-based AES_set_encrypt_key (compiled when neither OPENSSL_AES_CONST_TIME nor AES_ASM is defined).
key->rounds = 10 for 128-bit keys.
key->rounds = 12 for 192-bit keys.
key->rounds = 14 for 256-bit keys.
rk[0] = GETU32(userKey): the first key bytes become one big-endian-read u32 word stored natively, so on little-endian hosts each 4-byte word appears byte-reversed in RAM.
Non-MSVC GETU32(pt) = pt[0]<<24 ^ pt[1]<<16 ^ pt[2]<<8 ^ pt[3] (big-endian read).
u32 is unsigned int unless AES_LONG is defined.
The AES_ASM build of aes_core.c has an identical AES_set_encrypt_key (same rounds, same GETU32 words).
aarch64 asm builds compile aes_core.c without AES_ASM, so line 3045 is the C fallback there.
x86_64 asm builds do not compile aes_core.c (AES_set_encrypt_key comes from aes-x86_64.pl); the c-ref model on x86_64 corresponds to a no-asm build.
Opt-in OPENSSL_AES_CONST_TIME variant stores the schedule through a u64 pointer with a different word layout; it is not modelled.
__aesni_set_encrypt_key entry (aliased as aesni_set_encrypt_key).
$bits is the 32-bit register (%esi on SysV) so the rounds store writes 4 bytes.
movups ($inp),%xmm0 loads the user key as raw bytes.
$movkey %xmm0,($key): round key 0 is stored as raw bytes (movups), i.e. byte-identical to the key.
mov $9,$bits for 128-bit keys (comment: 10 rounds).
mov $bits,80(%rax) stores it at 240(key).
mov $11,$bits for 192-bit keys.
mov $13,$bits for 256-bit keys.
Readers use key->rounds at 240(key) directly as the aesenc loop count (one aesenc per decrement, then aesenclast).
aes_v8_set_encrypt_key entry (${prefix} = aes_v8).
vld1.8 {$in0},[$inp] loads the user key as bytes.
vst1.32 {$in0},[$out] stores round keys from the same vector; on little-endian the lanes keep the byte order, so rd_key holds raw bytes.
mov $rounds,#10 for 128-bit keys.
mov $rounds,#12 for 192-bit keys.
mov $rounds,#14 for 256-bit keys.
str $rounds,[$out] with $out advanced to key+240 ($rounds is w12, 4 bytes).
Readers load the rounds field from [key,#240].
HWAES_set_encrypt_key maps to aes_v8_set_encrypt_key on ARMv8 builds.
